This implies that the inhibition of SBK1 may modulate the activity of the latter enzyme, potentially through a direct or indirect regulatory pathway. The observed relationship is supported by a well-defined target interaction, with the final score indicating a plausible mechanistic link. The involvement of SBK1 as a mediator highlights the importance of kinase activity in the downstream effects of Oblonganoside C. The mechanism is consistent with a role in regulating nucleotide metabolism, as the ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase family member 6 is involved in the breakdown of nucleotides, suggesting a potential impact on cellular energy homeostasis.
